lead: Colour, background, font and text properties are ordinary CSS declarations: a property name plus a value, and most values can be written in more than one notation. The same tomato red is #FF6347, rgb(255, 99, 71) or hsl(9, 100%, 64%). Knowing all three matters because design tools export hex, brand guides quote rgb, and lightening a shade is easiest in hsl. Every sale badge, UPI app theme and IRCTC header you have seen is built from these few declarations.
prereq: You need: chapter 2.5 for declarations and units, and chapter 2.6 for what sits inside the box.

blocks.text: A colour property ends up as one RGBA value inside the browser, but CSS lets you write it several ways. Choose the notation that makes your intent clearest.

items: Keywords: about 140 names such as red, tomato and gold, plus rebeccapurple. Fine for a quick test, useless for a brand colour.
Hex: #RRGGBB is three pairs of hexadecimal digits from 00 to FF, giving 256 × 256 × 256 = 16,777,216 colours. The shorthand #RGB doubles each digit, so #F00 means #FF0000.
rgb(255, 99, 71): decimal channels 0 to 255. Modern CSS also accepts percentages and a fourth alpha value.
hsl(9, 100%, 64%): hue in degrees 0–360 (0 red, 120 green, 240 blue), then saturation and lightness as percentages. Change only lightness and you get a natural lighter or darker shade.
currentColor copies the element's own color value, so a border or an inline SVG icon always matches the text beside it.

blocks.where: V is the decimal channel value 0–255; d₁ is the value of the first hex digit (0–9, then A = 10 … F = 15) and d₂ the second. Example: FF = 16 × 15 + 15 = 255.

blocks.text: Alpha is a fourth channel written 0–1: rgba(255, 99, 71, 0.6) is 60% opaque. The separate opacity property also fades content, but it fades the whole element — text, border and every child box — while an alpha channel fades only the one colour it is attached to.

Every box has a background layer painted behind its content, its padding and its border, out to the outer edge of the border. background-clip: border-box is the default; set it to padding-box or content-box to pull the background in.

items: background-color: any colour value; the default is transparent.
background-image: url("logo.png") or a gradient. The image sits on top of the colour.
background-repeat: repeat (default), repeat-x, repeat-y or no-repeat.
background-position: two values, x then y — center, 50% 50%, right 10px bottom 20px.
background-size: auto, a length or percentage, cover or contain. cover fills the box and crops the overflow; contain shows the whole image and may leave gaps.
background-attachment: scroll (default) or fixed, which pins the image while the page scrolls.
background-clip: where the background is cut off: border-box (default, out to the outer border edge), padding-box or content-box.
background-origin: where background-position is measured from: padding-box (default), border-box or content-box.

blocks.text: A gradient is an image made of code. linear-gradient(90deg, #FF6347, gold) runs along 90 degrees, left to right, from the first stop to the last; radial-gradient(circle, #FF6347, gold) spreads out from the centre. A stop with a percentage, such as #FF6347 40%, tells the blend where to finish.
The background shorthand sets everything at once: background: #FF6347 url("logo.png") no-repeat center / cover fixed; Any order works, except that size must follow position after a slash.

sections.h3: Fonts: family, weight, and em versus rem

blocks.text: font-family takes a comma-separated stack, read left to right until one family is available. Multi-word names go in quotes, and the last item should be a generic family the browser certainly has: serif, sans-serif, monospace, cursive or fantasy. Example: font-family: "Noto Sans", Arial, sans-serif.
A web font arrives through @font-face, which gives a family name and points to a font file the browser can load. Add font-display: swap so readers see fallback text at once instead of a blank patch.

items: font-size: px, em, rem, % or keywords like small. The browser default is 16px.
font-weight: 100 to 900 in steps of 100; normal is 400, bold is 700. The font file must really carry the weight, or the browser picks the nearest.
font-style: normal, italic or oblique.
line-height: a bare number is best — 1.5 means 1.5 × this element's own font size — or a length such as 24px.

blocks.text: em and rem differ. In font-size, 1em is the parent's font size, so nested em sizes compound; 1rem is always the root (html) font size, so rem never compounds. For padding and margins, 1em means this element's own font size.

items: text-align: left, right, center or justify; justify stretches word spaces so both edges are flush.
text-decoration: underline, line-through, overline or none, with optional style, thickness and colour, e.g. underline wavy #FF6347.
text-transform: uppercase, lowercase or capitalize. It changes display only; an assistive reader may still spell out the original.
letter-spacing: 0.05em between characters; word-spacing: 4px between words; text-indent: 2em indents only the first line of a block.
text-shadow: x-offset y-offset blur colour, e.g. 2px 2px 4px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4). Commas stack several shadows.
white-space: normal (collapse spaces, wrap), nowrap (collapse but never wrap), pre (keep spaces and line breaks, no wrap), pre-wrap (keep both and wrap).

blocks.text: nowrap on a badge keeps SALE on one line; pre keeps a code listing exactly as typed.

figure.caption: The hex pairs FF, 63 and 47 are 255, 99 and 71, so the colour is rgb(255, 99, 71). Max 255 and min 71 give L = 64% and S = 100%, the green and blue channels give H ≈ 9°, and 60% opacity is the alpha value 0.6.

spec.aria: Three bars for the red, green and blue channels at 255, 99 and 71 on a 0 to 255 scale, with the range 184 marked; below, the steps to rgb(255, 99, 71), hsl(9, 100%, 64%) and rgba(255, 99, 71, 0.6).

examples.question: A sale badge uses the colour #FF6347. Convert it to rgb() and to hsl(), then write the same colour at 60% opacity.
steps: Split the hex into three pairs: FF, 63, 47.
For hsl, take max = 255 and min = 71; the range is 255 − 71 = 184.
Saturation: L is above 50%, so S = range ÷ (2 × 255 − max − min) = 184 ÷ (510 − 255 − 71) = 184 ÷ 184 = 1, that is 100%.
Hue: the largest channel is red, so H = 60 × (g − b) ÷ range = 60 × (99 − 71) ÷ 184 = 60 × 0.1522 = 9.13° ≈ 9°.
examples.check:
h = "FF6347"
r = int(h[0:2], 16)
g = int(h[2:4], 16)
b = int(h[4:6], 16)
print(r)
print(g)
print(b)
mx, mn = max(r, g, b), min(r, g, b)
L = (mx + mn) / 2 / 255
print(round(L * 100))
d = mx - mn
S = d / (2 * 255 - mx - mn) if L > 0.5 else d / (mx + mn)
print(round(S * 100))
H = 60 * ((g - b) / d) % 360
print(round(H, 1))

traps: Reading hex as decimal: FF is 255, not 15 and not 100. Each pair is base 16, with A = 10 … F = 15.
Giving alpha as 0–255. In rgba() and hsla() the alpha is 0–1, so 60% is 0.6.
Confusing opacity with alpha. opacity fades the element and all its children; an alpha channel fades one colour only.
Swapping cover and contain. cover fills the box and crops; contain shows everything and leaves empty space.
Forgetting that em compounds down nested elements while rem always measures against the root font size.

quiz.q: Write the colour #FF6347 in the other two common notations.
Name the five generic font families a font stack can end with.
Two elements have font-size: 20px and font-size: 30px. Both use line-height: 1.5. Why do their line heights differ in pixels?
quiz.a: A bare number multiplies the element's own font size: 30px and 45px. A length such as 1.5em would fix one value for both.

quiz.q: What is the practical difference between opacity: 0.5 on a card and background-color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5) on the same card?
quiz.a: opacity makes the card's text, border and children half transparent too; the rgba background only makes the background half transparent, so the text stays fully readable.

quiz.q: A paragraph inside a div has font-size: 1.25em. The div has font-size: 20px and the root is 16px. Give the paragraph size in px, and the size if the unit were 1.25rem.
A hero banner uses background: url(photo.jpg) center / cover no-repeat. On a wide screen the top of the photo is cut off. Explain why, and give one declaration that stops the cropping.
quiz.a: cover scales the image until it covers both the width and the height of the box, so the overflowing dimension is cropped; the centring splits that crop between top and bottom. Changing size to contain shows the whole photo but leaves empty strips, which the background-color then fills.

beyond: Not for the exam. Modern CSS adds color-mix() and relative syntax such as rgb(from #FF6347 r g b / 50%), and oklch() as a perceptually even colour space where equal lightness steps look equal. Large product teams store colour, spacing and type as custom properties on :root, which is one step from a design token system. Variable fonts pack many weights into one file. Search next: CSS custom properties, variable fonts, WCAG colour contrast, and the CSS Color Module Level 5.
